A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GIOROM by the same authors, despite retitling and substantial revision. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original Lagrangian simulation experiments, prediction errors, computational measurements, and sparsity analyses in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports original simulation results, reconstruction comparisons, computational benchmarks, and grid-resolution and sampling analyses in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v3 reconstructs fields through learned kernels evaluated over explicit radius-graph neighborhoods. v4 Section 3 and Appendix H.2 introduce density-normalized grid projection, stochastic Gaussian interpolation, feature encoding and decoding, and residual drift reconstruction. This substantially changes the reconstruction procedure. The interaction-network/transformer time-stepper and Euler integration remain essentially unchanged despite the new UPT framing.

E1.justification: Both versions cover water, sand, plasticine, elasticity, non-Newtonian fluids, and multimaterial dynamics, including the existing collision, melting, long-horizon, and high-resolution reconstruction scenarios. The additional v4 comparisons and grid studies use retained physical regimes and reconstruction tasks; they do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 2 adds CoLORA, DINo, CORAL, and a GKI reconstruction comparator alongside PCA, CROM, and LICROM. Table 3 adds GNS to the eight-system full-resolution comparison that was GIOROM-only in v3 Table 1. The earlier autoencoder water comparison and GINO/GNOT/IPOT/GNS time-stepper comparison remain in v4 Figure 3 and Table 6.

E3.justification: v4 introduces a reconstruction comparison reporting relative L2 error, Chamfer distance, timing, and memory at a stated 32 effective active degrees of freedom, with heuristic size matching. Static ROMs share a time-stepper, whereas DINo and CORAL train intrinsic neural ODE dynamics. New grid-resolution and computational-scaling sweeps add evaluation settings. Appendix H.2 also specifies Adam at 10^-3 for the revised kernel, replacing the earlier Adamax setup.

E4.justification: v4 adds cross-ROM reduced-space sensitivity curves in Figure 6, separates structure-building from function-evaluation costs in Figure 4, and tests grid resolution and sampling density in Figure 14. These substantially extend the questions investigated. Earlier message-passing, sampling-strategy, and extreme-sparsity analyses remain, while v3 Appendix J.3's kernel-cost sweeps are replaced.

E5.justification: v4 adds plus/minus reporting for relative errors in Table 2 and explicitly displays one-standard-deviation bands across test trajectories in Figure 14. v3 reports point estimates without corresponding uncertainty displays. This establishes added reporting of variation across cases, not an increase in training seeds or repeated runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial reconstruction, resource-use, and sensitivity results. In v3 Table 1 versus v4 Table 3, Water-3D rollout MSE changes from 0.386 to 38.6 and Sand-3D from 0.0025 to 0.25, both under the same displayed 10^-3 multiplier. These are revised entries, not established same-setting performance changes given the kernel revision and unexplained provenance. v3's detailed resolution-generalization and dense-upsampling timing tables are omitted; several other timing and ablation tables retain their values.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix B.3's RKHS-interpolation argument is removed. v4 introduces a normalized integral formulation and Appendix E's consistency analysis: i.i.d. sampling assumptions, Monte Carlo error decay, a smoothness-dependent grid-interpolation bound, a combined sampling/grid/neural error estimate, and a heuristic particle-coverage condition. The earlier GNN-as-integral-operator derivation remains in Appendix M.3.

C1.justification: The central claims of data-driven sparse Lagrangian simulation, local arbitrary-point reconstruction, and 6.6–32× input reduction remain. v4 clarifies and qualifies the contribution as hybrid sampling-based evolution directly in physical space with a separate spatial ROM, replacing the abstract's broader description of evolving reduced latent variables in v3.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive interpretations of regime-dependent performance: global bases can compete on stable geometries and outperform GIOROM under extreme sparsity. It explains grid failures through insufficient local particle/voxel support and interprets the grid-resolution plateau. These extend v3's connectivity and information-loss explanations, while the new coverage criterion is explicitly qualified as insufficient for a theoretical stability guarantee.

D1.justification: v4 supplies new reconstruction pseudocode and detailed Jax implementation information: a 64×64×64 grid, width-64 networks, four latent channels, eight stochastic paths, Gaussian width 0.42 in grid units, and a kernel-specific optimizer. These replace v3's radius-kernel implementation details. The abstract also expands the stated resource availability from code to code and data.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning against neural operators and ROMs through Section 2 and the new feature-comparison Table 1. It discusses UPT and Transolver applicability, reframes the retained time-stepper as a UPT-family adaptation, and adds references supporting CoLORA, CORAL, kernel regression, Monte Carlo integration, and spline approximation. These changes exceed citation-style or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v4 retitles the paper, changes GIOROM's expansion from Graph-Informed to Geometry-Informed, and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, positioning, and results narrative. Definitions move into the appendix, and experiments are reorganized around spatial parameterization and temporal computational efficiency. The restructuring is substantial independently of the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v4 adds the feature-comparison and per-dataset tables, computational and reduced-space plots, grid-ablation displays, and extensive baseline visual comparisons in Figures 17–20. It moves the architecture overview to the first page and relocates retained rollout figures and timing tables. Earlier displays are also removed or replaced, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3's ROM comparison largely centers on one water example, while its appendix exposes substantial reconstruction-memory costs. v4 makes these central tradeoffs much more assessable through a specified alternative reconstruction pipeline, systematic accuracy and resource comparisons across four regimes, and analyses identifying when competing global ROMs perform better. The implementation detail and trajectory-level variation reporting further strengthen the evidence. Heuristic reduced-size matching and unexplained rollout-value changes remain limitations, but the gains in evaluating and qualifying the central contribution are substantial.
